diffusion_ratio_question_0710pdt.code: turing_ratio/core.py, turing_ratio/sweep.py; artifacts/gpuops/turing_ratio_sweep.json; tests/test_turing_ratio.py (23 pass overall, 1 CUDA skip)
verified: codex counterexample reproduced with exact fractions: det(J-qD) = -21/25000, stable without diffusion; continuum d_c=1.0756 puts q=0.04 inside the band (0.0133,0.0686)
d_c = [(ae-2bc)+2sqrt(bc(bc-ae))]/a^2; Schnakenberg(a=.1,b=.9) d_c=8.5676 matches hand value
Brusselator: code matches closed form d_c=A^2/(sqrt(B)-1)^2 to 1e-9; stable iff B<1+A^2. d_c -> 1 as A grows and B -> 1+A^2: 1.134 / 1.031 / 1.021 at A=100 and 10% / 1% / 0.1% from the Hopf boundary

named kinetics over a log box [0.01,10]^2: min d_c Schnakenberg 5.92, Gierer-Meinhardt 5.92 (both the a->0 limit 3+2sqrt2=5.83 at trace->0, i.e. the Hopf boundary), Brusselator 1.93 at the box edge; Turing-region fraction of the box at d=1.1 is 0 for all three, at d=10 is 1.5%/2.2%/3.0% (Schn/Brus/GM)
diffusion_ratio_question_0710pdt.tradeoff_reading: Supported only in this sense: small d_c is reached only near the Hopf (stability) boundary of the kinetics, and at d=1.5 P(Turing | still stable under 5% entry perturbations) falls 0.38 -> 0.32 -> 0.21 as d_c/d goes 0.5-0.75 -> 0.75-0.9 -> 0.9-1.0 (ensemble E1). At d=10 the control shows P(Turing|stable)=1.0 until d_c/d>0.75.
NOT_established: a general tradeoff law: ensembles E1/E2 and the 5% perturbation are my arbitrary choices (E1 puts 0.7% of systems below d_c=1.1, E2 none)
nonlinear/subcritical outcomes (GPU/CPU PDE work not run)

mispredict_map_0745pdt.measured_cost: 10M stable activator-inhibitor systems x 4 ratio settings x 10 domain lengths + 240,000 exact-rational decisions = 30.3 s wall on CPU (2 threads)
mispredict_map_0745pdt.validation: exact Fraction decision (rational L/pi => rational q_n, sign of h(q_n) exact, no square roots) vs float64 vectorised: 0 disagreements in 240,000 decisions (120,000 per ensemble). Reproduces the interval fact: band q in (1/5,1/2) => mode n admissible iff L/pi in (n*sqrt2, n*sqrt5).
mispredict_map_0745pdt.gate_conclusion: The LINEAR mispredication map is CPU work (30 s for 10M systems); statistical error at N=5e6 is ~0.02-0.2 percentage points, so more samples buy nothing; 1e9 systems would be ~25 min of 2-thread CPU by linear scaling (unmeasured extrapolation). It is NOT a GPU workload. GPUs remain relevant only to the nonlinear/subcritical dual-solver piece, not run.
caveats: the headline level depends on the ensemble: at L=1.5*pi the mispredication rate is 5.2% (E1) vs 53.8% (E2) at d=10; shape (steep fall with L, non-monotone wiggles from integer mode counting) is consistent across ensembles; both ensembles are my arbitrary choices, not kinetics from the literature
L is in units where Du=1; the result is not scale-free: it depends on the absolute rates of the ensemble relative to the diffusion length sqrt(Du/a)
the primary's quoted 98.3% at L=pi -> 0.4% at L=20pi came from a different toy ensemble I did not see; mine give 80-100% -> 0.04-0.6%, same shape, not the same numbers
a principled ensemble (published kinetic models with units) is the scientific prerequisite for the map to mean anything about biology; that is not compute-limited
I did not check prior art (atlas-lean, Payan, Kurics-Menshykau-Iber, Ouchdiri) and did not touch Lean
